text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make their code easier to read and understand. For example, they may rename variables, split long functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate logic. The main goal is to keep the program's behavior exactly the same while making the code cleaner. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes are made instead of proper solutions. By refactoring regularly, teams can keep their projects healthy and make future changes faster and safer.
